summary: Monterey Fire Tower on Mount Wilcox, MA: CCC-built 1934 (several sources say 1935), 60-ft Aermotor MC-39, still in state use per a 2025 hiking post.

facts.design: 60-ft Aermotor MC-39 steel tower; original 7x7 wooden cab, new 10x10 cab and fence in 1966
facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

access.note: Fenced state fire tower on Mount Wilcox in Beartown State Forest; a hiking-history page says a visitor who asks permission while a guard is on duty might be invited up the tower, and that with no guard there is a fence and cameras

visit.trail_note: Park at the CCC Camp and walk the Mt. Wilcox Trail, a six-mile loop, per a 2025 hiking post

events.note: Erected by CCC Camp S-66; first day of operation April 1, 1934 per hiking-history page; Register description, Forest Lookouts and a 2025 hiking post say 1935
Massachusetts Geodetic Survey team visited and took measurements off the tower legs
Power line run and two-way radios installed
New 10x10 cab and chain-link fence built
An observer is listed for 1988 on a hiking-trail history page

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A hiking-history page gives 1934 (CCC Camp S-66, first operation April 1, 1934). The Register's description, the Forest Lookouts page and a 2025 hiking post give 1935. This record uses 1934 because it is the more specific date and names the first operating day; the 1935 figure from three other sources is noted.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts across four sources: three (Register, Forest Lookouts, and a 2025 hiking post) say 1935 and one hiking-history page says 1934. The 1934 date rests on that hiking-history page, which also gives April 1, 1934 as the first day of operation; verify against a Forest Service or DCR source if one turns up. The 2025 hiking post says the tower is still used today but does not say whether it is staffed. The hiking-history page's fence-and-camera note has no date in the text read, so it is not dated here. No notable fires found. The FFLA Facebook post on CCC Camp S-66 and the 2010s re-roof returned a login wall and was not read.
